domain: Transportation Systems / Institutional Coordination / Technology Standards
topic_summary: Analysis of the convention determining which side of the road vehicles drive on, focusing on right-hand driving as the dominant global standard. Examines the coordination mechanisms, path dependencies, and structural constraints that stabilize this convention despite its arbitrary origins.

key_entities: Right-hand traffic convention (global majority standard, ~165 countries)
Left-hand traffic convention (minority standard, ~75 countries including UK, Japan, India)
Vehicle manufacturing industry (produces region-specific steering configurations)
International standards bodies (Vienna Convention on Road Traffic 1968)
key_tensions: Network coordination benefit vs switching cost asymmetry (larger network has lower per-capita switching cost but higher aggregate cost)
Manufacturing standardization pressure vs installed base lock-in (global supply chain efficiency vs regional infrastructure investment)
key_mechanisms: Network effects: value of convention increases with adoption (coordination benefit scales with network size)
Switching cost enforcement: infrastructure (road signs, intersections, highway ramps) and vehicle fleet create exit barriers
Border management: physical infrastructure (lane crossovers, neutral zones) absorbs handedness transitions
key_absences: Historical origin analysis: why the split emerged (Napoleon's military standardization vs British Empire maritime tradition not examined in structural terms)
Safety differential data: whether right-hand vs left-hand driving has measurable accident rate differences controlling for other factors

axes.structural_delta: Self-reinforcing coordination equilibrium where deviation from local standard imposes immediate safety and infrastructure compatibility costs
axes.primary_observable: Switching cost magnitude (infrastructure replacement cost, vehicle fleet turnover cost, retraining cost) relative to coordination benefit; accident rate spike during hypothetical transition period
axes.selection_reason: Upstream mountain providing physical coordination constraint base; feeds both network and manufacturing axes

axes.structural_delta: Right-hand driving network is 2.2x larger than left-hand network, creating asymmetric switching incentives and standardization pressure
axes.primary_observable: Country count ratio (165 vs 75); population ratio; cross-border traffic volume at handedness boundaries; frequency of standardization proposals from minority-standard countries
axes.selection_reason: Distinct observable (network size ratio) from coordination lock-in; intermediate node linking coordination base to manufacturing extraction

axes.structural_delta: Global automotive supply chains extract efficiency gains by pressuring minority-standard markets to accept right-hand vehicles or pay premium for left-hand production runs
axes.primary_observable: Price differential for left-hand drive vehicles in right-hand markets and vice versa; model availability asymmetry; manufacturer statements on production line economics
axes.selection_reason: Highest centrality; downstream synthesis node with clear beneficiary/victim structure; captures extraction dynamic

axes.structural_delta: Physical infrastructure at handedness boundaries (lane crossovers, bridges, neutral zones) absorbs the coordination discontinuity, preventing it from propagating as systemic instability
axes.primary_observable: Design specifications and accident rates at specific border crossings (Thailand-Laos Friendship Bridge, Hong Kong-Mainland China crossings); infrastructure maintenance costs
axes.selection_reason: Distinct structural delta (spatial discontinuity management) and observable (border crossing design) from other axes; piton preventing coordination failure propagation

omegas.description: Is the right-hand majority a true Mountain (emerged from universal human factors like right-hand weapon dominance) or a Piton of historical contingency (Napoleon's military standardization happened to spread further than British maritime tradition)? If Piton, the current distribution is frozen accident rather than structural necessity.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) + F03 (Hasty Generalization)

omegas.description: Does handedness itself affect safety outcomes (e.g., right-hand driving safer for right-eye-dominant populations, or vice versa)? If measurable differential exists, the coordination equilibrium may be suppressing a safety-optimizing axis. Absence of this data in structural analysis is notable.

Do autonomous vehicles dissolve the coordination constraint by handling handedness transitions in software? If yes, the Mountain becomes a Scaffold (temporary coordination mechanism pending technological transition). Manufacturing extraction may intensify during transition as manufacturers control the software layer.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 1 (Operational Medium) — model analyzed within human-driver paradigm

omegas.description: Who bears switching costs in a hypothetical transition? If costs fall disproportionately on lower-income populations (older vehicle fleet, less access to retraining), the Rope of network size asymmetry may conceal a Snare where coordination pressure extracts from the economically vulnerable.

fracture_scan.notes: F03 detected: coordination_equilibrium_lock_in classified as Mountain but may be Piton of historical contingency if right-hand majority emerged from Napoleon's military standardization rather than universal human factors. Generated omega_historical_contingency to bound this uncertainty. No other fractures detected; four distinct axes survived independence testing with no merges required.
